summary: Run 6 of M1-S03 — the third § 4 test-only repair, after reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md run 9 (S2-F-14): 30/30 tests pass but coverage is 70.8% against the 75% floor, with Tier2WebhookFinalizer named as the gap (63 of 76 lines uncovered). Added artefacts/M1-S03/classes/Tier2WebhookFinalizerTest.cls (+ -meta.xml, API 67.0), a new file rather than more methods on Tier2WebhookQueueableTest, because apex-builder's own Escalation Rules forbid modifying a shipped file in place. Five methods call Tier2WebhookFinalizer.execute(FinalizerContext) directly as a plain synchronous call against a hand-implemented System.FinalizerContext stub, deliberately avoiding System.enqueueJob/Test.startTest()/Test.stopTest() of the parent job — deploy-order.md § 5 item 3 already recorded, from this same build, that letting the Queueable throw for real inside Test.stopTest() fails the test method, and skills/apex/apex-transaction-finalizers/references/code-examples.md documents the identical finding for its own worked Finalizer (its fix, a @TestVisible seam, cannot be applied here without touching the shipped class). The five methods cover: the ctx==null guard, the SUCCESS no-op, the transient-retry insert-and-re-enqueue path, the abandon-at-ceiling insert-and-stop path, and the existing-row update path. No 'permanent-failure' Finalizer branch was added — a permanent HTTP status never makes the Queueable throw, so Tier2WebhookFinalizer.execute() only ever sees SUCCESS for that case; that path is already asserted at the Queueable level. Shipped classes and all three pre-existing test classes are unchanged.
confidence_rationale: MEDIUM per GATES.md Gate D, with one risk this run names explicitly beyond the usual design-only baseline. Gate B: 0 unresolved symbols — every custom object/field/class this run's assertions touch (Case, Integration_Failure__c and its fields, Tier2WebhookFinalizer, Tier2WebhookQueueable.Tier2WebhookException, Tier2WebhookQueueable.pendingEnvelope) is grounded against files already in this step's artefacts. Gate C check 3 (compile) did not run — design-only build_mode, no target_org_alias, no offline Apex compiler in the sf CLI. Beyond that standard gap, this run's central technique — a test class implementing System.FinalizerContext directly — is UNVERIFIED against any source in this repo's corpus: no skill confirms or denies that customer code may implement that interface, and the one skill most specific to this exact problem (apex-transaction-finalizers) uses a different technique (a @TestVisible seam) for its own worked example rather than this one. If Tier2WebhookFinalizerTest.cls does not compile for this reason, the coverage gain this run claims does not exist and the fallback — a @TestVisible seam added to the shipped Tier2WebhookFinalizer.cls — is a shipped-code change explicitly out of this run's scope. What would raise this to HIGH is a green dry run with --test-level RunSpecifiedTests confirming both that the new class compiles and that coverage clears 75%, which no agent in this loop may perform.

findings.title: S2-F-14 addressed: Tier2WebhookFinalizer's retry/abandon/update branches now have direct unit tests
findings.detail: artefacts/M1-S03/classes/Tier2WebhookFinalizerTest.cls (new file) adds 5 test methods that call Tier2WebhookFinalizer.execute(FinalizerContext) directly against a hand-built System.FinalizerContext implementation, covering: the ctx==null guard, the SUCCESS no-op (asserting 0 rows and no enqueue), the transient-retry path (attempt=1, insert one Retrying row, exactly one re-enqueue), the abandon-at-ceiling path (attempt=MAX_ATTEMPTS, insert one Abandoned row, no re-enqueue), and the existing-row update path (attempt=2 with a pre-seeded row, update in place, Resend__c cleared, Request_Payload__c untouched). Whether this closes S2-F-14 in practice — i.e. whether coverage now clears 75% — is an org-side question; see S6-F-02.
findings.recommendation: Run reports/mock-deploy/... again with --test-level RunSpecifiedTests including this class to get the real coverage_pct. If it still falls short, the remaining gap is almost certainly the AsyncOptions/back-off lines and the chained-tail lines already named as untestable in deploy-order.md § 5 item 3 (ignored during Apex testing) — those are not addressable by any test.

findings.title: The core technique — implementing System.FinalizerContext in test code — is UNVERIFIED against this repo's corpus and has not been compiled
findings.detail: No skill under skills/apex/ states whether a customer-authored class may implement System.FinalizerContext. skills/apex/apex-transaction-finalizers/references/code-examples.md, the most specific and most authoritative source in this repo on Finalizer testing, solves the identical problem (reaching UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION without letting a real Queueable throw inside Test.stopTest()) with a @TestVisible decision seam instead — a technique unavailable here because Tier2WebhookFinalizer.cls is a shipped class this run is scoped not to modify. This run's approach is a reasoned extension consistent with FinalizerContext's documented four-getter shape (matching QueueableContext/BatchableContext, which are also not known to be customer-implementable but are also not documented as forbidden), not a cited, proven pattern. Gate C check 3 (compile) cannot run in this design-only build with no target_org_alias, so this cannot be confirmed here.
findings.recommendation: Before trusting this file's contribution to the milestone's coverage number, deploy it to a scratch org (sf project deploy start --dry-run --test-level RunSpecifiedTests) and confirm it compiles. If StubFinalizerContext fails to compile because System.FinalizerContext cannot be implemented by customer code, the fallback is a @TestVisible handle(...) seam added to Tier2WebhookFinalizer.cls itself (the apex-transaction-finalizers shape) — a shipped-code change, out of this run's scope, and a candidate for a follow-up apex-builder or apex-refactorer invocation once the requester approves modifying the shipped class. Either way, skills/apex/apex-transaction-finalizers should record the answer once known, so the next Finalizer test in this library does not have to re-derive it.

findings.title: No 'permanent-failure' branch exists inside Tier2WebhookFinalizer to test, and none was added
findings.detail: A permanent HTTP status (400/401/403/404/422) never makes Tier2WebhookQueueable.execute() throw (anyTransient stays false), so Tier2WebhookFinalizer.execute(ctx) only ever sees ParentJobResult.SUCCESS on that path — already covered by successResultTakesNoActionAndDoesNotConsumeTheEnqueueSlot in the new file and, at the level where the behaviour actually lives, by Tier2WebhookQueueableTest.permanentFailureRecordsTheAttemptAndDoesNotStamp and .authFailurePointsTheReaderAtThePrincipalGrant. The task's three named branches (transient-retry, abandon-after-last-attempt, permanent-failure) map to two real Finalizer branches plus one Queueable branch already covered elsewhere; adding a third Finalizer-level test under a 'permanent failure' name would have duplicated the SUCCESS test or asserted behaviour the shipped code does not have.
findings.recommendation: None needed — this is a mapping clarification, not a gap.

process_observations.observation: This build's own documentation had already named the exact gap this run closes: deploy-order.md § 5 item 3 recorded 'the throw → Finalizer → re-enqueue path itself is deliberately uncovered' back at run 2/3, with the correct reason attached (an unhandled exception in a Test.stopTest()-run job fails the test). Nothing about the S2-F-14 finding was a surprise — the prior run's honesty about what it left uncovered, and why, is exactly what let this run go straight to a real fix instead of re-discovering the constraint from scratch.

skills/apex/apex-transaction-finalizers/references/code-examples.md documents its own worked Finalizer hitting the identical test-design problem this step's Finalizer has, with a full worked test class showing the @TestVisible-seam answer. Reading it end to end (not just the SKILL.md summary) is what surfaced both the exact risk to avoid and the shape of a safe alternative.

This is the fourth distinct root cause found on this one step across five runs (S2-F-04/F-05 compile faults, S2-F-11 test-identity, S2-F-12 factory over-assignment, now S2-F-14 coverage) plus a fifth, S2-F-13, found at the milestone level but rooted in this step's design. Each was individually narrow and each fix was individually small, but the pattern — an org-executing dry run finding something no offline checker could see, five times on the same step — says the step type this library calls 'automation' (trigger + Queueable + Finalizer + tests, in one invocation) is under-checked by static tooling relative to its actual failure surface, not that this particular step was unusually troubled.

Whether System.FinalizerContext can be implemented by customer Apex is the load-bearing assumption of this entire run and it is not settled by anything in this repo. It reads as very likely correct by analogy to QueueableContext/BatchableContext, but 'very likely correct by analogy' is not the same bar this library otherwise holds itself to (a cited apexdev/apexrefguide line, or an UNVERIFIED tag with an org-confirmation recommendation — the second of which this run applied, both in the new file's header and in deploy-order.md § 0d).
